results.title: Armed robbers flee Paris De Beers store on motorcycles after jewellery heist
results.content: Four black-clad individuals sped away from De Beers jeweller in Paris's second arrondissement Thursday morning after stealing hundreds of thousands of euros worth of luxury goods at gunpoint. Police are searching for those responsible.

results.title: ICRC: We are currently classifying the highest number of armed conflicts since the Second World War
results.content: François Picard is pleased to welcome the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Mirjana Spoljaric. “You may consider war a human condition,” argues Spoljaric. “But brutality, barbarity, is not a human condition.” Her warning recalls the fundamental premise of the 1949 Geneva Conventions: even in war, there can be no lawless space, and certain red lines must never be crossed.

results.title: France's social safety net: Can it afford to be so generous?
results.content: Created in the aftermath of World War II, France's social security system has become one of the pillars of French society, providing everything from healthcare and family benefits to pensions. But with an ageing population and mounting deficits, this ambitious model is facing a major financial test. We look at how the system works, why it is so deeply valued by the French and whether the country can afford to keep its promise of protecting everyone – from cradle to grave.

results.title: ICRC: We are currently classifying the highest number of armed conflicts since the Second World War
results.content: François Picard is pleased to welcome the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Mirjana Spoljaric. “You may consider war a human condition,” argues Spoljaric. “But brutality, barbarity, is not a human condition.” Her warning recalls the fundamental premise of the 1949 Geneva Conventions: even in war, there can be no lawless space, and certain red lines must never be crossed. Spoljaric warns that the international rules established to protect civilians are being progressively weakened amid proliferating armed conflicts, technological transformations and the retreat of diplomacy.

results.title: Mississippi elects its first African American to US Senate since Reconstruction
results.content: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black US Senator since Reconstruction. His narrow victory, confirmed on November 11 after prolonged ballot counting, marks a major political shift in the conservative state. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

results.title: France: Five men on trial for murder of anti-drug activist Amine Kessaci's brother
results.content: In France, the trial of five men accused of murdering the brother of anti-drug activist Amine Kessaci is under way. Amine Kessaci, originally known as an environmental activist, became a prominent figure in the fight against drug-related crime after losing two of his brothers to violence linked to drug trafficking. The defendants face the possibility of life imprisonment. The verdict is expected on Monday, November 16. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley tells us more.

results.title: Huang powers and bankrolls AI revolution: Nvidia CEO caught between 'a rock and a very hard place'
results.content: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of France's Institute of Digital Sovereignty. Benhamou examines the intersection of traditional espionage, geopolitical rivalry and the extraordinary concentration of power within the global AI industry. Discussing allegations surrounding Nvidia's leadership, he describes the chipmaker as "the banker of the global AI system," a striking characterization that captures the company's importance not merely as a semiconductor manufacturer, but as a central actor in the economic and technological infrastructure underpinning the AI boom. "Because humans stay humans." results.title: 🔴 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to step down after affair
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after affair raises national security concerns
results.content: Nvidia announced on Thursday that CEO Jensen Huang was stepping down following revelations that he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. The company's chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for Huang's successor.

results.title: Can the fight against climate change be good for business?
results.content: Industries across the globe are seeking to reduce their carbon footprint and become more sustainable. To do so, many are turning to employees with specific credentials. According to LinkedIn's Global Green Skills Report 2026, workers with green skills are being hired at more than 1.5 times the rate of the wider workforce.

results.title: Midterms: Democrat Colom claims historic win in Mississippi
results.content: Scott Colom has become the first Black person to win a Senate race in Mississippi since 1874 and the first Democrat to do so since 1982 after being declared the victor in a razor-edge election on Wednesday. The win is a stunning upset in one of the country’s most reliably red states, adding to what were already sweeping gains by the Democrats at the midterms.

results.title: War photographer Patrick Chauvel: 'People have lost faith in the press'
results.content: One of France's top war photographers, who has a 50-year CV of taking pictures in and around conflicts across the planet, has spoken to FRANCE 24 about his concerns that people have lost faith in the press. He notes that journalists are only looking for the truth. Patrick Chauvel has produced nearly 380,000 photographs, from Vietnam to Cambodia, from Afghanistan to Palestine, from Lebanon to Ukraine. He says he wants to take people by the hand to show them how the press works and why.

results.title: 🔴Live: Putin offers to evacuate civilians from eastern Ukraine's Kostiantynivka
Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon: Displaced families struggle to cope
results.content: In Lebanon, more than 360,000 people are still displaced after months of war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to the UN. Along the border, the Israeli army claims to be fighting the Iran-backed militant group but now occupies 6 percent of Lebanese territory and is wiping entire villages off the map. In the border area, we meet families living in makeshift housing. Many fear they may never go home.

results.title: Throwing cow dung: Diwali celebrations take an unusual turn in southern India
results.content: The third day of Diwali was marked in a memorable way on Wednesday in Gummatapura, a hamlet located in India's Tamil Nadu state. Local men and boys threw cow dung at each other to celebrate the festival of Gorehabba which honours Lord Beereshwara, a God worshipped by locals. Believed to be around 300 years old, the festival attracts tourists from across India and further afield.

results.title: Rare pictures from Marilyn Monroe's final shoot on auction in Paris
results.content: Prints from the personal collection of photographer Bert Stern are going under the hammer in Paris on December 2, marking the first time his private archive has been offered for sale. Among the highlights of the auction are iconic photographs of Marilyn Monroe, taken just weeks before her death.

results.title: Two French guards collapse as Macron welcomes Slovak president
results.content: Two members of France's elite Republican Guard collapsed almost simultaneously outside the Elysee Palace as President Emmanuel Macron welcomed his Slovak counterpart, according to televised images and a presidential source.

results.title: Paraguayans get some savings back after banking collapse disrupted economy
results.content: Paraguay's Central Bank said Wednesday, November 11, it had partially returned savings to all eligible Ueno Bank depositors locked out of their accounts when it collapsed last week. The digital bank's takeover on November 3 triggered massive protests across Paraguay and led to the impeachment and arrest of ex-president Santiago Pena, who is linked to Ueno.

results.title: European leaders gather in Dublin to discuss Ukraine's security, and their own
results.content: Leaders from more than 40 European countries gathered in Dublin on Thursday, November 12, for a summit focused on the continent’s fragile security, amid a new US-backed effort to revive talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war. The meeting of the European Political Community brought together heads of state and government from European countries and the UK, as well as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.

results.title: New York: Deadly building collapse in Brooklyn
results.content: A three-storey building collapsed in New York’s Brooklyn on Wednesday, killing at least two and injuring 17 others. The building, in the Flatbush area, collapsed at around 4pm local time, and tumbled into a neighbouring construction site, with the cause of the collapse still under investigation.

results.title: Thousands of schools evacuated in Italy as bomb threats spread across Europe
results.content: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger". The threats come after a series of hoax bomb alerts across Europe in recent weeks, which have prompted growing concern about the possibility of an escalation in hybrid warfare.

results.title: COP31: Climate disruption puts farmers and global food supplies under pressure
results.content: As delegates gather in Turkey for the COP31 climate conference, discussions are focusing on emissions and climate targets. But humanitarian agencies are highlighting another urgent consequence of climate disruption: growing food insecurity. With the return of El Niño adding to concerns over extreme weather and its impact on food production, the Food and Agriculture Organisation is calling for food systems to be placed at the heart of climate action.

results.title: Nvidia board weighing up whether or not to oust CEO Jensen Huang
results.content: Nvidia's board is holding a late-night meeting to decide whether or not to oust CEO Jensen Huang after a second extramarital affair was revealed. The scandal has revealed a major weakness at the heart of the chipmaker sitting at the heart of the AI boom: the lack of a clear succession plan. We take a closer look.

results.title: DR Congo's Tshisekedi signs referendum law amid fears of third-term bid
results.content: DR Congo President Félix Tshisekedi paved the way for a constitutional amendment on November 10 by signing a law authorising a referendum. The move comes amid concerns that he could seek a third term in office, with opposition figures accusing him of manoeuvring to remain in power.
